According to Table 2, the analysis of the nomination compliance for the four processing plants
to meet the demand indicates that Maurel and Prom had a 100% compliance rate, while TPDC
Madimba had a compliance rate of 94%, TPDC Songo Songo had a compliance rate of 91%, and
Songas Plant had a compliance rate of 94% during the review period. The lower compliance rate
was due to unplanned and emergency maintenance of production wells and plant facilities, as
well as changes in downstream customer demand.
(iii) Natural Gas Processing Plants Availability
During the review period, the Authority monitored the operations and maintenance activities
of natural gas processing plants to ensure maximum availability. The availability of M&P gas
processing plant was 99.89%, TPDC Songo Songo gas processing plant was 98.07% while
Songas’s plant at 99.55% and TPDC Madimba gas processing plant was 100% availability. The
average plant availability for the period under review is as shown in Table 3. TPDC Songo Songo,
Songas and M&P processing plants availability were below 100% due to planned and unplanned
shutdowns that occurred during the reporting period.

(iv) Processing Plants Capacity Utilisation
Table 4 provides a comparison of the annual average capacity utilisation in percentage for
TPDC Madimba, TPDC SSI, Songas, and M&P natural gas processing plants for FY 2020/21, FY
2021/22, and FY 2022/23. The analysis shows that there was an increase in utilisation for each
year, although the increment was minimal. Therefore, it is crucial to make strategic investments
to increase the utilisation of these processing plants.

7. NATURAL GAS SUPPLY AND DEMAND BALANCE
In FY 2022/23, natural gas consumption and supply increased compared to the previous financial
year due to an increase of new households’ connection, industries, CNG-Vehicles, power plants
and the increase of power generation from existing gas-fired power plants. The summary of
natural gas customers per category is provided in Table 26.
Table 26: Natural Gas Customer Categories

2021/22 11 52 970 1 8 3

Natural gas demand is expected to increase due to implementation of new distribution projects,
such as Mwenge-Mbezi trunckline for supplying natural gas to commercial centres and industries.
Also, due to ongoing gas supply connection to Saphire Floating Glass industries at Mkuranga and
increasing number of CNG-Vehicles.
7.1 Natural Gas Supply
The total natural gas supplied during FY 2022/23 was 81,067.15 MMscf compared to 72,533.56
MMscf for FY 2021/22 and 60,619.12MMscf in FY 2020/21. The supply increment from FY
2021/22 to FY 2022/23 was 11.77%, which is minimal compared to a 33.73% increment from
FY 2020/21 to FY 2022/23. The comparison of the natural gas supply from the four plants is as
illustrated in Figure 34 and Table 27.
